admission.justification: Two costs meet here — a repeated parse on every heartbeat and an unbounded enumeration — and both are invisible in functional tests that only check the rows. The read-counter and two-size cases measure the work a pass does.

applicability: The acquisition path that reads the native stores and the discovery that enumerates receipts and held folders.
conditions: Initialized, completed file-backed views skip acquisition on a quiet pass. First observation, a full refresh or the relevant invalidation acquires them; cold or unfinished held and pause acquisition also resumes on the existing heartbeat. Permissions derive from retained host facts and stall clocks update on every pass.
Enumeration is budgeted per call and resumes where it stopped, keeping its continuation state bounded.
Completed quiet file-backed refreshes reread no native source.
exclusions: Re-reading every native store on each heartbeat.
Retaining continuation state without a bound.
Presenting a resumed or shed walk as a complete census.

evidence: notes/reports/reviewer/267804e5-dd71-51e8-8f1d-d975effaaeaf/role-launch/round4/L190-fix-verification-R4.json#L190-R1-F11; DirectoryWalk bounds actual entries, including noise, to each allowance with retained iterators. Held root/receipt/folder acquisition shares256entry steps, with bounded walk count/depth and sticky incompleteness on shedding; pause acquisition has its explicit256entry per-pass budget and bounded heap. Partial acquisition resumes on existing heartbeat without fresh host poll; complete idle observations skip native acquisition. Four size subcases fail on pre-repair enumeration work and pass on candidate, with quiet and eventual-complete controls. Exact counts/fixture work evidence are not substituted for aggregate native CPU/RSS/reload proof, which remains F01.

statement: Retained native inputs and resumable bounded discovery avoid repeated quiet work and scale within explicit per-refresh allowances.
